title: Attested Policy Passport v0.2
description: Signed, identity-anchored, multi-plane graph projection of a KG edge. v0.2 introduces graph_refs (plural): per-plane provenance keyed by plane name, superseding the single graph_ref of v0.1. The passport is a condensed graph extract — sufficient to reconstruct a digital twin of the edge's governance context within milliseconds of the artifact landing in Git. The proof is an Ed25519 signature over the JCS-canonicalized body with `proof` excluded. v0.1 consumers remain valid against v0.1 passports; v0.2 is a wire-format version bump, not an in-place mutation.

passport_version.description: Passport wire-format version. 0.2 introduces multi-plane graph_refs.

spiffe_id.description: Source workload identity. SPIFFE is an attestation about the workload, not its identity; the workload URN in network_binding is the stable anchor.

compliance_scope.description: Compliance requirements this edge satisfies, e.g. PCI-DSS-v4:req-1. In v0.2 these labels are duplicative convenience only — the authoritative controls linkage is graph_refs.controls. Retained for v0.1 reader compatibility and human scan-ability.

ownership.description: Accountability + routing context. Not part of edge identity or enforcement. All fields optional.

transport.description: L4 transport — part of edge identity. NOT the app protocol.

port_unspecified.description: True when no port could be resolved — an admission of ignorance, NOT permission. See APP-000 §6, APP-090.

port_wildcard.description: True when an author deliberately granted every port on this path. See APP-090.

app_protocol.description: Descriptive L7 label(s). Excluded from edge_id so observed L4 flows still match declared claims.

graph_refs.description: *** v0.2 CORE CHANGE — per-plane provenance. Each key is a plane (per the multi-plane PAP ADR); each value is either a provenance object or an explicit absence marker. The architecture plane is always required: an edge with no architectural authoring has no business holding a passport. Other planes are required or waivable per the platform's plane policy for the environment class. A plane key that is entirely missing from this object means MISSING — required-but-unauthored — and is a drift finding, distinct from absent-by-policy which is a governed statement. ***

architecture.description: CALM-authored architectural provenance. edge_id here is the canonical L4-tuple hash (APP-000). Always required.

controls.description: OSCAL-authored controls provenance. node_id points at a controls-plane node: kg://oscal/control/<control-id>/<imp-req-id>. Resolving it yields the implemented-requirement, its parameters, and the catalog chain up to the source framework (NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS). node_version is REQUIRED here (MP-43): OSCAL intake (MP-16) means controls-plane nodes are authored, so STALE_ATTESTATION is computable and a missing digest is a defect, not 'no evidence yet'. This is a per-plane requirement — architecture keeps node_version optional.

business_intent.description: TOSCA-authored business/orchestration provenance. node_id points at a business_intent-plane node: kg://tosca/policy/<template>/<policy>. node_version is REQUIRED here (MP-46): TOSCA intake (MP-21) means business_intent-plane nodes are authored, so — exactly as for controls — STALE_ATTESTATION is computable by content and a missing digest is a defect, not 'no evidence yet'. Per-plane requirement, matching controls; architecture stays on the base plane_ref.

expires_at.description: Unix epoch seconds. No renewal → edge lapses → rule becomes a contraction candidate.

algorithm.description: Signature scheme. `ed25519` is the crawl/demo default (deterministic). `ecdsa-p256` (ES256) is used when signing with a SPIRE X509-SVID leaf key, which is EC P-256 (APP-080).

canonicalization.description: RFC 8785 canonical JSON, then sign. Signature covers the body with `proof` excluded — including the full graph_refs object, so per-plane provenance is inside the signed envelope.

plane_ref.description: Provenance for one plane. node_id is the stable graph GUID for the governing node in that plane. authored_by is who authored the node (distinct from proof.issuer, who signed the passport) — the two-provenance discipline of v0.1 now holds per-plane.

node_id.description: Stable plane-node GUID. Architecture plane uses kg://edges/v1/<sha256>; controls plane uses kg://oscal/control/<control-id>/<imp-req-id>; business_intent uses kg://tosca/policy/<id>. Pattern is plane-scheme-open so new planes mint their own scheme without a schema bump.

node_version.description: Content hash of the plane node AS READ at signing time. Makes STALE_ATTESTATION computable by content rather than by clock: the referent has moved iff the node's current hash differs from this one. Immune to skew, backdated authoring, and no-op edits — the edge_id discipline applied one level up. Optional on this base type; tightening to required happens per-plane once that plane has authored graph nodes (see plane_ref_versioned, used by controls as of MP-43 and business_intent as of MP-46). It stays optional where a required flag would force a fabricated digest for a node that does not yet exist — and a fabricated digest makes a stale passport look fresh, the exact failure this field prevents. Architecture remains optional: its ref carries the edge_id itself, already a content hash.

plane_ref_versioned.description: A plane_ref whose node_version is mandatory. Used by planes that have authored graph nodes — controls, as of OSCAL intake (MP-16 / MP-43), and business_intent, as of TOSCA intake (MP-21 / MP-46) — so STALE_ATTESTATION is always computable by content for a valid passport. The per-plane boundary is deliberate rather than a schema-wide flip: a plane joins this def only when its intake authors real nodes, because requiring node_version before then would force every emit to fabricate a digest for a node that does not exist, and a fabricated digest makes a stale passport look fresh. Architecture stays on the base plane_ref (its node_id is the edge_id, already a content hash).

plane_absent.description: Explicit absence: this plane is deliberately not authored for this edge, waived by platform plane policy. 'Not here on purpose' — a governed statement, distinct from a missing key which means required-but-unauthored (a drift finding).

waived_by.description: The platform plane-policy rule that waives this plane for this environment class, e.g. platform-policy/plane-requirements-v1#dev-waives-business-intent.
